revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Party Favor Bags
revealWordProblem.text: Reginald is making party favor bags. He has 24 stickers and 36 erasers. He wants every bag to have the same number of stickers and the same number of erasers, with none left over, and he wants to make as many bags as possible. What is the greatest number of bags he can make, and how many stickers and erasers go in each bag? Explain your reasoning.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: The greatest number of bags is the GCF of 24 and 36. The common factors of 24 and 36 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12, so the GCF is 12. Reginald can make 12 bags, each with 24 ÷ 12 = 2 stickers and 36 ÷ 12 = 3 erasers, with none left over.

vocabulary.definition: A factor of a whole number divides it evenly, with no remainder. For example, 3 is a factor of 12 because 12 ÷ 3 = 4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un factor de un número entero lo divide exactamente, sin dejar residuo. Por ejemplo, 3 es un factor de 12 porque 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — What is the greatest common factor (GCF)?
conceptIntro.intro: A factor is a number that divides another number evenly, with nothing left over. The greatest common factor is the biggest factor that two numbers share. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: The GCF is the largest number that divides BOTH numbers with no remainder.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I want the GCF of 24 and 36. First I list the factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24.
Next I list the factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36.
Now I circle the factors in BOTH lists: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. These are the common factors.
The biggest one is 12, so the GCF of 24 and 36 is 12. I check: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 and 36 ÷ 12 = 3. Both are even, so 12 works.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Let's find the GCF of 8 and 12. What are the factors of 8? (1, 2, 4, 8.)
What are the factors of 12? (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12.) Which numbers are in both lists? (1, 2, 4.)
Which shared factor is the largest? (4.) So the GCF of 8 and 12 is 4.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

youDo.title: Now you try — with support

approaching.stem: What is the GCF of 8 and 12?
approaching.explanation: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The largest common factor is 4.
choiceFeedback: 2 does divide both 8 and 12, but it isn't the greatest number that does. List all the factors of 8 and of 12 and look for a bigger one they share.
8 is a factor of 8, but check 12 ÷ 8 — it does not come out even. A common factor has to divide both numbers with nothing left over.
24 is a number that both 8 and 12 divide into, which makes it a common multiple, not a common factor. A factor is never larger than the number it belongs to.
hints: GCF means the GREATEST factor the numbers share. You need a number that divides BOTH 8 and 12, not just one of them.
List all the factors of 8, then all the factors of 12. Circle the numbers that appear in both lists and pick the largest.
Factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, and 8. Now write out the factors of 12 and circle every number that shows up in both lists.
hintsEs: 7x y 3x tienen la misma variable x, así que son términos semejantes y se pueden combinar.
Suma los coeficientes; la x se queda exactamente igual: no se eleva al cuadrado ni se multiplican los coeficientes.
Calcula 7 + 3 y pon esa suma delante de x.
hintsEs.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el máximo común divisor (MCD) de 8 y 12?
hintsEs.explanationEs: Factores de 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factores de 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. El mayor factor común es 4.
hintsEs: MCD significa el MAYOR factor que los números comparten. Necesitas un número que divida a AMBOS, 8 y 12, no solo a uno.
Escribe todos los factores de 8 y luego todos los de 12. Encierra los números que aparecen en ambas listas y elige el mayor.
Los factores de 8 son 1, 2, 4 y 8. Ahora escribe los factores de 12 y encierra cada número que aparezca en las dos listas.

hintsEs.stem: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 5?
hintsEs.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Both share the factor 5, and 5 is the largest shared factor.
choiceFeedback: 10 and 12 have a GCF of 2 — 5 divides 10 but not 12. Check that 5 divides BOTH numbers in the pair you pick.
This pair does share a factor, but test 5 against 6 first: 6 ÷ 5 leaves a remainder, so 5 cannot be a factor of both.
5 divides 20 evenly, so it is easy to stop here — but check 8 ÷ 5 too. Both numbers have to work.
hints: You're hunting for a pair where 5 divides BOTH numbers — and where no bigger number divides both.
Quick check: a number divisible by 5 ends in 0 or 5. After that test, confirm 5 is the LARGEST factor the pair shares.
Look at 10 and 12 first: 10 ends in 0, but does 5 divide 12 evenly? If not, that pair is out — test the other pairs the same way.
hintsEs.explanationEs: 9n + 2n = 11n. La constante 4 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 11n + 4.
hintsEs: Hay dos términos con n (9n y 2n) y una constante solitaria (4) sin pareja.
Combina solo los términos semejantes; la constante 4 se queda aparte en tu respuesta.
Suma 9n + 2n sumando 9 + 2. El 4 conserva su propio lugar al final.
hintsEs.explanationEs: 9n + 2n = 11n. La constante 4 no tiene término semejante, así que se queda. Resultado: 11n + 4.
hintsEs.stemEs: ¿Cuál pareja de números tiene un MCD de 5?
hintsEs.explanationEs: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Los dos comparten el factor 5, y 5 es el mayor factor común.
hintsEs: Buscas una pareja en la que 5 divida a AMBOS números, y donde ningún número mayor divida a los dos.
Revisión rápida: un número divisible entre 5 termina en 0 o en 5. Después confirma que 5 sea el MAYOR factor que comparte la pareja.
Mira primero 10 y 12: el 10 termina en 0, pero ¿divide el 5 al 12 exacto? Si no, esa pareja queda fuera; prueba las demás igual.

hintsEs.stem: What is the GCF of 14 and 21?
hintsEs.explanation: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. The largest common factor is 7.
choiceFeedback: 14 divides itself, but 21 ÷ 14 leaves a remainder, so 14 can't be the GCF. The GCF must divide both numbers evenly — test the factors of 14 against 21.
3 divides 21 evenly, but 14 ÷ 3 leaves a remainder. Test every candidate against both numbers before you choose.
1 divides every whole number, so it is always a common factor — but you are looking for the greatest one. Keep comparing the two factor lists.
hints: Both 14 and 21 appear in times tables you know. Which multiplication facts build each number?
Write each number as a multiplication fact, then compare: which factor shows up in both facts?
Factors of 14 are 1, 2, 7, and 14. Now list the factors of 21 and find the greatest number that lives in both lists.
hintsEs.explanationEs: 6x y 2x son términos semejantes porque los dos tienen la misma variable (x) elevada a la misma potencia (1).
hintsEs: Los términos semejantes necesitan exactamente la misma variable elevada exactamente a la misma potencia.
Compara dos cosas en cada pareja: la letra y el pequeño exponente sobre ella. Ambos deben coincidir exactamente.
Prueba la primera pareja: 6x y 2x — ¿misma letra? ¿misma potencia? Si ambas coinciden, son semejantes.
hintsEs.explanationEs: 6x y 2x son términos semejantes porque los dos tienen la misma variable (x) elevada a la misma potencia (1).
Factores de 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factores de 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. El mayor factor común es 7.
hintsEs: Tanto 14 como 21 aparecen en tablas de multiplicar que ya conoces. ¿Qué multiplicaciones forman cada número?
Escribe cada número como una multiplicación y luego compara: ¿qué factor aparece en las dos?
Los factores de 14 son 1, 2, 7 y 14. Ahora escribe los factores de 21 y busca el mayor número que esté en ambas listas.

hintsEs.stem: What is the GCF of 9 and 15?
hintsEs.explanation: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. The largest common factor is 3.
choiceFeedback: 1 is a common factor, but it isn't the greatest — 9 and 15 share a bigger factor. List the factors of 9 (1, 3, 9) and check which also divide 15.
9 is a factor of 9, but 15 ÷ 9 leaves a remainder, so 9 is not shared by both numbers. Check each candidate against both.
45 is a number that 9 and 15 both divide into — that makes it a common multiple. Factors go the other direction: they divide into the numbers.
hints: Don't settle for 1 — most pairs share something bigger. What number multiplies into both 9 and 15?
List the factors of each number: 9 has just three factors and 15 has four, so the lists are short to compare.
Factors of 9 are 1, 3, and 9. Now write out the factors of 15 and pick the greatest number that appears in 9's list too.
hintsEs: Identifica los términos semejantes: 5a y 2a comparten la variable a. El 3 no tiene variable.
Combina los términos con a sumando sus coeficientes; el 3 se lleva sin cambios.
Suma 5 + 2 para el coeficiente de a y luego escribe la constante 3 después.
hintsEs.explanationEs: Factores de 9: 1, 3, 9. Factores de 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. El mayor factor común es 3.
hintsEs: No te quedes con el 1: casi todas las parejas comparten algo mayor. ¿Qué número multiplica para formar 9 y también 15?
Escribe los factores de cada número: 9 tiene solo tres factores y 15 tiene cuatro, así que las listas son cortas de comparar.
Los factores de 9 son 1, 3 y 9. Ahora escribe los factores de 15 y elige el mayor número que también esté en la lista del 9.

hintsEs.title: Spot the Common Mistake — Not the Greatest

workedExample.label: List factors of 12
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 12

workedExample.label: List factors of 30
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 30

workedExample.label: Choose the GCF
workedExample.work: Sam circles 3 and says the GCF of 12 and 30 is 3.
workedExample.workEs: Sam encierra el 3 y dice que el MCD de 12 y 30 es 3.

hintsEs.correctWork: The common factors of 12 and 30 are 1, 2, 3, and 6. Sam stopped at 3, but the GREATEST common factor is the largest one, which is 6. So GCF(12, 30) = 6.
hints: Sam listed the factors correctly. Look at the shared factors: 1, 2, 3, 6. Did Sam pick the largest one?
The GCF is the GREATEST common factor. The biggest number in the shared list 1, 2, 3, 6 is 6.
hintsEs.titleEs: Detecta el error común: no es el mayor
hintsEs.explanation: Sam's two factor lists are correct, and the factors that 12 and 30 share are 1, 2, 3, and 6. The mistake happens at the last step: 3 really is a common factor, but it is not the greatest one. The GCF is the largest number in the shared list, so GCF(12, 30) = 6.
hintsEs.explanationEs: Las dos listas de factores de Sam están correctas, y los factores que comparten 12 y 30 son 1, 2, 3 y 6. El error ocurre en el último paso: 3 sí es un factor común, pero no es el mayor. El máximo común divisor (MCD) es el número más grande de la lista compartida, así que GCF(12, 30) = 6.
hintsEs.correctWorkEs: Los factores comunes de 12 y 30 son 1, 2, 3 y 6. Sam se detuvo en 3, pero el MÁXIMO común divisor es el más grande, que es 6. Así que MCD(12, 30) = 6.

hintsEs.stem: A teacher has 36 pencils and 48 erasers. She wants to make identical supply bags with no items left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
hintsEs.explanation: GCF(36, 48) = 12. She can make 12 bags, each with 3 pencils and 4 erasers.
choiceFeedback: Is that really the biggest factor they share? Check your list again.
4 does divide both 36 and 48 evenly, so it is a common factor — it just is not the greatest one. Keep looking for a larger number that still divides both.
Are you sure that's the GREATEST? Check the smaller factors too.
hints: 'Identical bags with nothing left over' is the clue: the number of bags must divide 36 AND 48 with no remainder.
Find the greatest number that divides both 36 and 48 — list the common factors and take the largest one.
List the factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Now test which of these also divide 48 evenly, and take the greatest.
hintsEs.stemEs: Una maestra tiene 36 lápices y 48 borradores. Quiere armar bolsas de materiales idénticas sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es la mayor cantidad de bolsas que puede armar?
hintsEs.explanationEs: MCD(36, 48) = 12. Puede armar 12 bolsas, cada una con 3 lápices y 4 borradores.
hintsEs: 'Bolsas idénticas sin que sobre nada' es la pista: el número de bolsas debe dividir a 36 Y a 48 sin residuo.
Busca el mayor número que divida a 36 y a 48: escribe los factores comunes y toma el más grande.
Escribe los factores de 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. Ahora prueba cuáles de ellos también dividen a 48 exacto y toma el mayor.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake — GCF or LCM?

workedExample.label: List factors of 8
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 8

workedExample.label: List factors of 20
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 20

workedExample.label: Choose the answer
workedExample.work: Jordan multiplies 8 × 20 = 160 and says the GCF of 8 and 20 is 160.
workedExample.workEs: Jordan multiplica 8 × 20 = 160 y dice que el MCD de 8 y 20 es 160.

onLevel.correctWork: Multiplying the two numbers does not give the GCF. The GCF is the largest factor the numbers SHARE. The common factors of 8 and 20 are 1, 2, and 4, so the GCF is 4 — and a factor can never be larger than the numbers themselves.
hints: A factor of 8 cannot be bigger than 8. Is 160 a factor of 8 and 20, or did Jordan multiply instead?
Find the common factors of 8 and 20: 1, 2, 4. The greatest one is 4, so GCF(8, 20) = 4.
onLevel.titleEs: Detecta el error común: ¿MCD o mcm?
onLevel.explanation: Jordan multiplied 8 × 20 to get 160, but multiplying two numbers produces a common multiple, not a common factor. A factor of 8 can never be larger than 8 itself. The factors 8 and 20 share are 1, 2, and 4, so GCF(8, 20) = 4.
onLevel.explanationEs: Jordan multiplicó 8 × 20 y obtuvo 160, pero multiplicar dos números produce un múltiplo común, no un factor común. Un factor de 8 nunca puede ser mayor que 8. Los factores que comparten 8 y 20 son 1, 2 y 4, así que GCF(8, 20) = 4.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Multiplicar los dos números no da el MCD. El MCD es el factor más grande que los números COMPARTEN. Los factores comunes de 8 y 20 son 1, 2 y 4, así que el MCD es 4 — y un factor nunca puede ser mayor que los propios números.

onLevel.stem: Mission Control must split 24 oxygen tanks and 36 ration packs into identical crew pods with none left over. What is the GCF of 24 and 36?
onLevel.explanation: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The greatest shared factor is 12, so 12 pods can be filled equally.
choiceFeedback: 6 divides both 24 and 36, but it isn't the biggest number that does — stopping too early makes the pods smaller than they could be. Keep checking common factors above 6.
8 divides 24 evenly, but 36 ÷ 8 leaves a remainder. A common factor has to work for both numbers.
72 is a number that 24 and 36 both divide into, so it is a common multiple. A factor divides into the numbers instead.
onLevel.stemEs: El Control de Misión debe repartir 24 tanques de oxígeno y 36 paquetes de raciones en cápsulas idénticas para la tripulación, sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es el MCD de 24 y 36?
onLevel.explanationEs: Factores de 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factores de 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. El mayor factor compartido es 12, así que se pueden llenar 12 cápsulas por igual.
hints: The greatest common factor is the largest number that divides both amounts evenly, with nothing left over.
Write out every factor of 24 and every factor of 36, then look at which numbers show up on both lists.
Factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Start the list for 36 the same way — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ... — and find the largest number that appears on both lists.
hintsEs: El máximo común divisor es el número más grande que divide exactamente a las dos cantidades, sin que sobre nada.
Escribe todos los factores de 24 y todos los factores de 36, y luego observa qué números aparecen en las dos listas.
Los factores de 24 son 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Empieza la lista de 36 de la misma forma — 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, ... — y busca el número más grande que aparezca en las dos listas.

onLevel.stem: The astronaut crew has 40 solar cells and 60 battery cells to load into matching storage bins with nothing left over. What is the GCF of 40 and 60?
onLevel.explanation: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The greatest shared factor is 20, so 20 bins can be filled equally.
choiceFeedback: 10 is a common factor of 40 and 60, but not the greatest one. Check whether a number larger than 10 also divides both 40 and 60 evenly.
4 divides both 40 and 60, so it really is a common factor — but it is not the greatest one. Look further down your list for a bigger shared factor.
120 is a common multiple of 40 and 60, not a factor. A factor of 40 can never be larger than 40.
onLevel.stemEs: La tripulación de astronautas tiene 40 celdas solares y 60 celdas de batería para guardar en contenedores iguales sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es el MCD de 40 y 60?
onLevel.explanationEs: Factores de 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Factores de 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. El mayor factor compartido es 20, así que se pueden llenar 20 contenedores por igual.
hints: You need the largest number that divides both 40 and 60 evenly — that is what the greatest common factor means.
List the factors of the smaller number first. The GCF can never be larger than 40, so that list sets your ceiling.
Factors of 40 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Test them against 60 starting from the largest and stop at the first one that divides 60 with no remainder.
hintsEs: Necesitas el número más grande que divide exactamente a 40 y a 60: eso es el máximo común divisor.
Primero escribe los factores del número menor. El MCD nunca puede ser mayor que 40, así que esa lista marca el límite.
Los factores de 40 son 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. Pruébalos con 60 empezando por el mayor y detente en el primero que divida a 60 sin residuo.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — The Wrong Mission Number

workedExample.label: The problem
workedExample.work: Split 12 oxygen tanks and 18 ration packs into the most equal crew pods with none left over.
workedExample.workEs: Reparte 12 tanques de oxígeno y 18 paquetes de raciones en la mayor cantidad de cápsulas iguales sin que sobre nada.

workedExample.label: List factors of 12
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 12

workedExample.label: List factors of 18
workedExample.labelEs: Haz la lista de factores de 18

workedExample.label: Choose the number of pods
workedExample.work: Cadet Rio says 36 pods, because 36 is the smallest number that both 12 and 18 divide into.
workedExample.workEs: El cadete Rio dice 36 cápsulas, porque 36 es el número más pequeño entre los que 12 y 18 caben exactamente.

onLevel.correctWork: Cadet Rio found the LCM (least common multiple = 36), but making equal groups with none left over needs the GCF (greatest common factor). The common factors of 12 and 18 are 1, 2, 3, 6, and the greatest is 6. So Mission Control can fill 6 equal pods, each with 2 oxygen tanks and 3 ration packs.
hints: Splitting supplies INTO equal groups with none left over uses the GCF, not the LCM. The GCF is a factor that divides both numbers, so it must be 12 or smaller, not 36.
List the common factors of 12 and 18: 1, 2, 3, 6. Which one is the GREATEST? That is the number of pods.
onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: el número de misión equivocado
onLevel.explanation: Cadet Rio found 36, which is the least common multiple of 12 and 18, not the greatest common factor. Splitting supplies into equal groups with none left over needs a number that DIVIDES both counts, so it can never be bigger than 12. The common factors are 1, 2, 3, and 6, so Mission Control fills 6 pods with 12 ÷ 6 = 2 tanks and 18 ÷ 6 = 3 packs each.
onLevel.explanationEs: El cadete Rio encontró 36, que es el mínimo común múltiplo de 12 y 18, no el máximo común divisor. Repartir los suministros en grupos iguales sin que sobre nada necesita un número que DIVIDA a las dos cantidades, así que nunca puede ser mayor que 12. Los factores comunes son 1, 2, 3 y 6, así que Control de Misión llena 6 cápsulas con 12 ÷ 6 = 2 tanques y 18 ÷ 6 = 3 paquetes cada una.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: El cadete Rio encontró el MCM (mínimo común múltiplo = 36), pero hacer grupos iguales sin que sobre nada requiere el MCD (máximo común divisor). Los factores comunes de 12 y 18 son 1, 2, 3, 6, y el mayor es 6. Así que el Control de Misión puede llenar 6 cápsulas iguales, cada una con 2 tanques de oxígeno y 3 paquetes de raciones.

onLevel.explanation: Amara's factor lists and her list of common factors (1, 2, 4) are all correct. The error is in the last step: she chose 2, but the GCF has to be the greatest of the shared factors, which is 4. So the GCF of 16 and 28 is 4, not 2.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las listas de factores de Amara y su lista de factores comunes (1, 2, 4) están correctas. El error está en el último paso: eligió 2, pero el MCD tiene que ser el mayor de los factores compartidos, que es 4. Entonces el MCD de 16 y 28 es 4, no 2.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: MCD = 4 (el mayor de los factores comunes, no cualquier factor común). Amara encontró bien los factores comunes, pero eligió 2 en lugar del más grande, 4.

onLevel.prompt: A farmer has 54 apples and 36 oranges. She wants to make gift baskets where every basket has the same number of apples and the same number of oranges, with none left over. Find the greatest number of baskets and explain how you used GCF to solve this.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: The GCF of 54 and 36 is ___ because ___. So the farmer can make ___ baskets, each with ___ apples and ___ oranges.
hints: Re-read: every basket identical, nothing left over. The basket count must divide 54 AND 36 — and be the GREATEST number that does.
Find GCF(54, 36) using factor lists or prime factorization. Then divide 54 and 36 by that GCF to fill each basket.
Start: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Multiply the primes both share to get the basket count, then divide to fill baskets.
onLevel.explanation: Every basket has to be identical with nothing left over, so the number of baskets must divide both 54 and 36 — and 'the greatest number of baskets' means the GCF. Since 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 and 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, they share 2 × 3 × 3 = 18. The farmer makes 18 baskets, each with 54 ÷ 18 = 3 apples and 36 ÷ 18 = 2 oranges.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada canasta debe ser igual y no puede sobrar nada, así que el número de canastas tiene que dividir a 54 y a 36, y 'la mayor cantidad de canastas' significa el MCD. Como 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 y 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3, comparten 2 × 3 × 3 = 18. La agricultora arma 18 canastas, cada una con 54 ÷ 18 = 3 manzanas y 36 ÷ 18 = 2 naranjas.
onLevel.promptEs: Una agricultora tiene 54 manzanas y 36 naranjas. Quiere armar canastas de regalo donde cada canasta tenga la misma cantidad de manzanas y la misma cantidad de naranjas, sin que sobre nada. Encuentra la mayor cantidad de canastas y explica cómo usaste el MCD para resolverlo.
hintsEs: Vuelve a leer: cada canasta idéntica y sin que sobre nada. El número de canastas debe dividir a 54 Y a 36, y ser el MAYOR que lo hace.
Halla MCD(54, 36) con listas de factores o con factorización prima. Luego divide 54 y 36 entre ese MCD para llenar cada canasta.
Empieza: 54 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 3 y 36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3. Multiplica los primos que comparten para hallar el número de canastas y luego divide.

hintsEs.commonMistake: A common mistake in Greatest Common Factor is confusing it with the Least Common Multiple: some students list the MULTIPLES of both numbers and pick the smallest shared one (getting an answer bigger than either number, like 72 for 24 and 36) instead of listing FACTORS and picking the largest one they share (12). Remember: the GCF splits numbers INTO equal groups, so it can never be bigger than the smaller of the two numbers.

connect.scenario: A baker is making gift boxes with cookies and brownies. She has 48 cookies and 32 brownies. She wants every box to have the same number of cookies and the same number of brownies, with none left over.
connect.promptQuestion: How does the GCF help the baker? How many boxes can she make?
connect.prompt: The baker can make ___ boxes because the GCF of 48 and 32 is ___.

check.stem: What is the GCF of 48 and 32?
check.explanation: 48 = 2⁴ × 3 and 32 = 2⁵. The shared prime factors are 2⁴ = 16, so the GCF is 16. 8 divides both but it is not the greatest.

check.stem: How many cookies go in each box?
How many brownies go in each box?
check.explanation: 32 brownies ÷ 16 boxes = 2 brownies per box. Each box gets 3 cookies and 2 brownies with nothing left over.

connect.modelAnswer: The GCF of 48 and 32 is 16, so the baker can make 16 identical boxes. Each box gets 48 ÷ 16 = 3 cookies and 32 ÷ 16 = 2 brownies, with none left over. Any larger number of boxes would not divide both amounts evenly.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: What is the GCF of 18 and 27?
exitTicket.explanation: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. The factors they share are 1, 3, and 9, so the GCF is 9 — the GREATEST shared factor, not just any common factor (that rules out 3). Six divides 18 but not 27, so it is not actually a common factor at all, and 18 is one of the original numbers, not a factor shared with 27.
exitTicket.hint: Think through the problem step by step.
choiceFeedback: 3 divides both, but is there a LARGER shared factor of 18 and 27?
Does 6 divide 27 evenly? Recheck your common factors.
18 doesn't divide 27 — the GCF must divide BOTH numbers.
hints: The GCF must divide BOTH 18 and 27 evenly — and it has to be the GREATEST number that does, not just any shared factor.
List every factor of 18, then every factor of 27, and compare the two lists before you pick.
Write 18's six factors (from 1 up to 18) and 27's four factors. Circle the shared ones and choose the largest circle.

questions.explanation: 6x and 2x are like terms because they both have the same variable (x) raised to the same power (1).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a prime number?
questions.explanation: 17 has exactly two factors: 1 and 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, and 9 = 3 × 3, so they are all composite.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 18?
questions.explanation: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so 2 × 3 × 3 is the prime factorization.

questions.stem: What is the prime factorization of 30?
questions.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All three factors (2, 3, 5) are prime, so 2 × 3 × 5 is the prime factorization.
